::: {.callout-note}
**This document is for the facilitator's eyes only.** It is rendered with the workshop's website but left out of the navbar, so no other page links to it. It holds the run sheets, the answer keys, the crib facts and the contingency ladders of the full-day format of the Europeanisation and the economy case study (`live/day.qmd`), which works on aggregate data only and is taught in the workspace, with the web slides showing each step, and the sessions of the multi-day format, whose second day is the full-day format. The pages of a format give the participants no times, and every time is here. The slides, the browser lab, the class chart and the other notes on the formats are in the section on [the slides and the pipeline](#decks-and-pipeline).
:::

## The formats {#the-three-formats}

The facilitator chooses the format; participants do not choose, and the home page describes the formats without offering a choice. Each track is an ordered route through the pages of the workshop's website, reached from the Formats section of the home page, with a docked sidebar of its own (`_sidebar.yml`) that lists its exercise page and its tools, and a slides page embedding the slides on which it runs. Name the track of a delivery in `delivery.track` of `_variables.yml`, and the callout of the home page links it. The decisions behind the formats, and the order in which their material was built, are in `formats-2026-10-27.md` in the planning folder beside the AR4DS websites (`../_planning/`).

| Format | Track | What it holds | Slides |
|---|---|---|---|
| Part-day | `tracks/short/` | Two halves of eighty and ninety minutes, with the cells of the tasks on the slides: the three Rs and the SCORE robustness study (Aczel et al. 2026), the paper and its record, the estimand statement, the reproduction of C6HJR, KQXUE or 018OL, the three models and few clusters; then the menu with its survey decisions first, the code behind the menu, Task 4 and the class chart, the multiverse and the curve of 864, reading a curve, the critics and preregistration, and the replication by its verdict | `live/short.qmd`, web slides written for the session |
| Full-day | `tracks/day/` | Four parts: the claim and credibility, the estimand and the causal graph, the reproduction, and robustness with Tasks 4 and 5 | `live/day.qmd`, web slides whose hands-on slides carry the cells of the five tasks |
| Multi-day | `tracks/long/` | Day 1 open research and the tools, the same for every case study; day 2 the full-day format; day 3 the methods of the case study and the report of each participant | the slide decks of day 1 on the AR4DS website, `live/day.qmd` on day 2, and the slide decks of day 3 |
| Self-taught | `tracks/independent/` | Five stages, from credibility and the three Rs to a project of your own | the full slide deck, `slides/full.qmd` |

The full-day format works on aggregate data only. The participants do the tasks in the workspace, in their IDE, while I run each step on the web slides, whose cells run R in the browser; the slides and the browser lab carry the work of anyone whose installation fails. The parts of the full-day format are of unequal length: the reproduction is the shortest, and robustness the longest, because it holds the two tasks with submissions. The clock times below are drafts; set them for the delivery and paste them into the day plan and the joining instructions, because the pages of the participants give no times.

| Segment | Clock (GMT, draft) |
|---|---|
| Part 1 | 10:00–11:30 |
| Break | 11:30–12:00 |
| Part 2 | 12:00–13:15 |
| Lunch | 13:15–14:15 |
| Part 3 | 14:15–15:25 |
| Break | 15:25–15:55 |
| Part 4 | 15:55–17:45 |

## The delivery lifecycle {#delivery-lifecycle}

Between deliveries the landing page advertises no upcoming delivery. Scheduling a delivery takes the steps below, and resetting after one takes two.

**Scheduling.**

- [ ] Fill the `delivery:` block in `_variables.yml` (date, venue or platform, event, mode, registration URL), set `track` to `short`, `day` or `independent`, and set `active: 'true'`. Re-render and push, and the landing page shows a "Next delivery" callout. Set `active: 'false'` again afterwards.
- [ ] Decide recording. If recording: talk segments only, announced at the start of each recorded stretch, paused for hands-on segments. Nothing in the day depends on the recording either way.
- [ ] Optionally create the preregistration mirror form from `../_planning/prereg-form-spec.md` and paste its URL into `_variables.yml`. The preregistration block is the primary record and the form only a backup, so skipping the form loses nothing.

**Resetting, after a workshop.**

- [ ] Export the responses Sheet (File → Download → CSV) and commit it as a date-stamped snapshot (for example `data/class_results_2026-11-06.csv`); refresh `data/class_results.csv` as `facilitator/live-results-setup.md` describes if you want the archived class visible on the workshop's website.
- [ ] Clear (or archive to a second tab) the old rows in the live Sheet so that the chart opens almost empty for the next class. **Do not touch the Form, the Worker, or the field schema.** The pipeline works, and only the rows change from one class to the next.

## The preparation of participants {#preparation}

The page "Before the day" or "Before the workshop" of each format lists these steps. The pages give no times, so if the joining instructions need them, put them there.

| Step | Full-day | Multi-day |
|---|---|---|
| The background page | required | required |
| The slides used on the day or the browser lab, opened once, with the cells of Task 1 run (the R engine of the lab takes 10 to 30 seconds to load on a slow connection, and the slides longer, since they load the packages of every task) | required | – |
| R, an IDE and the workspace, until `R/check_setup.R` reports no failure | required | required |
| Getting started with R (`tools/r.qmd` on the AR4DS website) | required | required |
| The Eurobarometer files, downloaded under a GESIS account of the participant | – | required |
| The exercise page of the format, sections 1 to 3 of the module on panel data, and the reading on inference of the Specification curve page (`curve.qmd#inference`) | recommended | – |
| The modules on the IDE, on Quarto and on Git and GitHub (AR4DS website) | recommended | the reading of days 1 and 3 |

## The week before

- [ ] Send joining instructions: the before-the-day page of the track, the links of the slides used on the day and of the browser lab with the instruction to open the slides or the lab once, and the [background page](../background.qmd) as the pre-reading. For the full-day and multi-day formats add the setup page, with the request to run `R/check_setup.R` until it reports no failure, and the module Getting started with R; for the multi-day format add the download of the Eurobarometer files.
- [ ] Confirm that the four Task 2 instructions on the Part 3 slide "Task 2 of the robustness study" match your own Task 2 report (copy in `../_planning/osf_source/moreh_rep_vAPR2025/`), which is the source that the slide quotes.
- [ ] Check that the three OSF deposits of Hands-on 3b load logged out (osf.io/vycgd, osf.io/nz7ka, osf.io/6zqct), and that osf.io/h7432 shows the five components of the robustness study.
- [ ] Click once through the tab switching of Part 4 (slides, the specification menu with its decision map, the Class results page, the reading on inference of the Specification curve page, and back), so that the order is familiar on the day.

## The night before

- [ ] Render the workshop's website and push; if it is published, confirm that the Pages build completes on GitHub Actions.
- [ ] **Cold load of the slides**: open the web slides `live/day.qmd` in a private window on the connection typical of the venue; time the wait until its cells show Run Code, a wait that includes the packages of every task; run the cells of Hands-on 1 and of one analyst of Hands-on 3, the cells that I drive on the day.
- [ ] **Browser lab cold load**: open the live page of `lab.qmd` in a private window on the connection typical of the venue; time the load of the webR engine; run the cells of Task 1 and the cells of all three analysts in Task 3. The cell of 018OL that installs lme4 and lmerTest downloads about 32 MB, so time that too.
- [ ] **The live results loop** (full setup and checks in `facilitator/live-results-setup.md`): submit one anonymous test row through the Form in a private window, confirm that it reaches the Sheet and that the Worker returns the sheet as CSV, press *Run Code* on the live [Class results]({{< var live-results-url >}}) page and find the test mark. Then delete the test row.
- [ ] **The preregistration loop**: complete the preregistration cell of the slides or the browser lab with a dummy specification, run `prereg()`, `build_model()` and `run_spec()`, and check the output. If the mirror form exists, submit one dummy row and delete it.
- [ ] Prepare the catch-up card and the day plan (texts below) for the screen.
- [ ] Charge everything.

## Opening the room {#opening-the-virtual-room--30-minutes-before}

- [ ] Put the URL of the workshop's website, the URL of the slides, the browser-lab URL, the cheatsheet URL and the day plan with its times on the screen as people arrive.
- [ ] Say that a raised hand brings help at any point, for a question or for a machine that is stuck.
- [ ] Share the slides, whose cells I run for each step; keep the specification menu with its decision map and the Class results page ready in other tabs.
- [ ] If recording: announce it now and state what is and is not recorded.

## Driving the slides {#deck-navigation}

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| space, right arrow, clicker | next slide. **Always exactly one slide** – the slides are set to linear mode so that no clicker press can skip a segment |
| **`d`** | switch between the **full** and the **lean** slides, live. In lean mode the optional slides are taken out: every key skips them and the count drops |
| **`]`** and **`[`** | jump to the **next or previous part** |
| **`g`** | **jump bar**: type a few letters of any slide title, press Enter |
| **`s`** | speaker view (notes, timer, next slide) |
| **`f`**, **`esc`** | fullscreen, slide overview |

**The readout, top right,** has two lines. The first names the part and gives the position in the part and overall (for example `PART 3`, `8/24`, `90/148`). The second is a badge that is always present and shows the state of the slides:

| Badge | Means |
|---|---|
| green **full** | the optional runs are switched on, and this slide is part of the main flow |
| burgundy **optional** | the optional runs are switched on, and this slide belongs to one of them. The figure beside it is your position inside that run – `3/12` |
| amber **lean** | the optional runs are switched off |
| a burgundy **dot** before the amber badge | lean mode, and an optional run has been lifted out right here – either the slide you are on is the last before it, or the first after it. Press `d` if the class wants it |

The slides of the full-day format lift no optional run into their main flow (`core-runs: []`), and the full slide deck lifts both runs, the methodological tutorial and the multiverse tutorial; add `?depth=0` to the address to open a slide deck in lean mode. The first slide of each optional run has a small grey link at the top right, which says how many slides the run contains and where the main flow resumes.

## The slides and the pipeline {#decks-and-pipeline}

**The browser lab.** The browser lab is a page that runs R in the tab of the browser and holds the five tasks of the exercise beside the workspace, the same tasks as the two sets of web slides, as the fallback when the slides do not load. It is live: it loads the data of the case study, which are small (a panel of 43 KB), and runs the code of the tasks on them, each fit in a fraction of a second. The causal-graph task prints the answers that the pipeline computed with dagitty for the graphs that the cell offers, because dagitty cannot run in the tab; any other graph goes to the workspace.

**The slides.** The slide decks are assembled from segments: the full slide deck of the self-taught format and the web slides of the full-day format share the segments in `slides/_segments/case/`, and the web slides add their own in `live/_segments/`, among them the hands-on slides that carry the cells of the browser lab. A slide deck is a list of `{{< include >}}` lines with its own agenda, aims and part dividers. In the segment files, every slide of an optional run is marked with `.deepdive` and a `run` attribute (`methods` or `multiverse`). A slide deck lists the runs that belong to its main flow under `core-runs:` in its YAML, and `slides/core-runs.lua` strips the `.deepdive` mark from those headings, so `nav-tools.html` neither hides them on the `d` key nor badges them as optional. A run that is not listed stays optional: it is hidden in lean mode and has the escape-hatch link on its first slide. The segment files contain R chunks with labels, and knitr refuses a duplicate label, so each slide deck includes each segment at most once. Edit the segment files for content, or the file of the slides for order and framing, and render the slides on their own (`quarto render live/day.qmd`). A change to a segment needs every slide deck that includes it rendered again (`grep -l "europeanisation/_x.qmd" slides/*.qmd live/*.qmd`). The project render fails at its final move step on this machine, so slide decks are rendered one at a time.

**The part-day format.** The part-day format is three hours in two halves, with no Task 2 at the keyboard (each participant writes the estimand statement in their notes), no Task 5, and one submission to the class chart, the explored analysis of Task 4. Its slides, `live/short.qmd`, carry the cells of Tasks 1, 3 and 4 through the Quarto Live extension, so that the class and the facilitator work inside the same slides, with the browser lab as the fallback. They are not assembled from the segments of the slides of the full-day format: they are a custom set of slides in `live/_segments/`, one segment for each block of the run, with the clock of the block in a comment at the head of the segment, so that an event can edit them block by block and set its own title and subtitle in the YAML. They live in a folder of their own, with `live/_metadata.yml` keyed `live-revealjs`, because the `format: revealjs` key of the metadata of `slides/` would render them twice (root notes, Gotchas). The reproduction offers the three analysts of the lab: the slides load the two packages of 018OL when they are opened, and on the lab route its cell downloads them, about 32 MB, which the track page says. The helpers of the lab (`try_spec()` and the rest) are one file, `_includes/_lab-helpers.qmd`, included by the lab and by the slides. The first delivery proposed is the ESRA–WAPOR conference of July 2027 in Paris, for an audience of survey researchers, which is why the menu is taught with its survey decisions first and two slides show the easystats code behind the workshop. The [run sheet](#run-sheet-short) gives the clock.

**The slides of the full-day format.** The full-day format and day 2 of the multi-day format run on `live/day.qmd`, web slides with the content of the plain slides that they replaced. Their hands-on slides carry the cells of the browser lab: Task 1 and the warm-up, Task 2, the three reproductions of Task 3, Task 4, the placement and Task 5. The participants work in the workspace; I run each step on the slides, and each hands-on slide names, in one line, the chunk or the file of the workspace in which the step lives. A participant whose installation fails opens the slides in a tab of their own and works in their cells, or in the browser lab. The slides load the packages of every task when they open, lme4 and lmerTest included, so that no cell downloads during the day. They live in `live/` beside the slides of the part-day format, and both include the helpers of the lab, with the graph functions of Task 2, from `_includes/_lab-helpers.qmd`.

**Pages that the formats share.** Every track starts from the [background page](../background.qmd), which tells the original study, SCORE and its robustness study, the five reanalysts with an assessment of their choices, and the conversion lesson on how the robustness study turned their statistics into one effect size. The specification menu is taught as the full set of fourteen decisions, on the page [Specification menu](../menu.qmd), whose first section is the [decision map](../menu.qmd#map), with the curve of 864 specifications as the subset that a review judged justifiable for this claim. The helpers of the browser lab and of the workspace refuse an option that is off the curve, with the one-sentence reason recorded in `data/menu_options.csv` and the page that teaches the option. Every result is classed by standard errors clustered by country with the CR2 correction and Satterthwaite degrees of freedom; the specification of C6HJR (t = −3.804, r = −0.242) has a CR2 p of 0.0504 on 9.8 degrees of freedom and is not significant under that rule, which is worth saying before anyone asks. The [run sheet of the full-day format](#run-sheet-one-day) has its timings.

**The class chart.** The chart on the Class results page reads the rows of the shared results Form whose labels have the frozen format of the case study, `explore: [tag] <spec>` or `declared: [tag] <spec>`, with no word for the case study after the tag. The labels of the other case studies of AR4DS carry that word, and the chart draws their rows as unclassed diamonds, so clear the Sheet between deliveries of different case studies. Each workspace keeps its own tag in `.class-tag`, so ask a cohort to choose one nickname and to pass it as `nickname = "..."` throughout. A chart keeps the rows of earlier deliveries until the sheet is cleared.

## Run sheet – the part-day format {#run-sheet-short}

The part-day format runs on `live/short.qmd`, slides written for it that carry the cells of the tasks, as two halves of eighty and ninety minutes with a break of ten. It has no Task 2 at the keyboard (each participant writes the estimand statement in their notes), no Task 5, and one submission to the class chart, the explored analysis of Task 4; the reproduction offers C6HJR, KQXUE and 018OL, one slide each, and Hands-on 2 takes three slides (the reference call, two variations, the submission). Participants run the cells on their own machines while the facilitator drives the same slides on the projector; the browser lab holds the same tasks as a page of the workshop's website, for anyone whose slides will not load. The class chart stays on the projector from Task 4 to the close. Ask participants to open the slides the evening before on the machine they bring, so that the browser holds its files, and carry a phone hotspot. Clear the results Sheet before the session.

### Cutting order and never cut {#cuts-short}

For a slot of two and a half hours, cut in this order: the slide on where the idea of the multiverse comes from; the critics to one slide; the three models to one; the record in SCORE at speed; the code behind the menu to one slide. **Never cut:** the five results, the estimand statement, the reproduction, Task 4 with the class chart, the bet before the decomposition, and robustness against replicability on this paper.

| 1:05 | What the curve leaves out and inference literacy (12′) | The four points; description and inference; dependence; the permutation design; the discussion beat. | Think; argue. | The target answer: "we cannot say until we know what chance produces on these dependent data". |
| 1:17 | Replication with new data (5′) | The verdict of the SCORE replicability study again, and the decisions that a replication fixes in advance, the fifteenth answer category among them. | Listen. | The verdict only; the figures of the replication stay off the slides. |
| 1:22 | Critics, one correct analysis, what preregistration settles (6′) | The three positions; the one correct analysis and how anyone would identify it; the two columns of preregistration. | Listen. | – |
| 1:28 | Archiving and the public record (4′) | Archiving and registering, with the preregistration of the robustness study; the three OSF addresses; the templates; the eight AsPredicted questions. | Listen. | If time is short, one slide. |
| 1:32 | Hands-on 5: the preregistration and the declared run (15′) | Each participant completes the block, runs `prereg()` and renders the report, or copies the cell in the slides, before running anything; then build, run, `report_result()`. | Declare, build, run, submit. | Never cut the declaration. |
| 1:47 | Close and feedback (3′) | Two points from the literature; what you take with you. | Feedback. | End on time. |

### Cutting order and never cut {#cuts-one-day}

- **Part 1** – trigger 0:24: the open-research practices table in one sentence per row.
- **Part 2** – trigger 0:18: the crash course drops the selection-and-feedback slide to a sentence. Trigger 1:08: Task 2 to demonstration only.
- **Part 3** – trigger 0:30: the three reproduced models in one slide. Trigger 0:52: Hands-on 3b on my screen.
- **Part 4** – trigger 0:10: the methodological tutorial stays off, or keeps its core slides (outcome, claim alignment, estimators, what fixed effects adjust for). Trigger 0:20: Task 4 shortens to two `try_spec()` calls and a submission – but everybody still submits. Trigger 0:38: skip the multiverse tutorial, keep "what the curve leaves out". Trigger 1:17: the replication and the critics in one slide each.

**Never cut:** the five-analyst reveal; the estimand statement; the half-built graph and its adjustment set; the reproduction; the table of CR2 tests; the Task 4 submission; the bet before the decomposition; the preregistration.

## The multi-day format {#run-extended}

The multi-day format is three days, with the full-day format as its second day (`tracks/long/`). The first day is the same for every case study of AR4DS and is given from slide decks of the AR4DS website; the third day teaches the methods of this case study, from the panel to the respondents, and ends with the report of each participant. A two-day version drops the third day. Participants download the Eurobarometer files before the workshop, under their own GESIS accounts. At the end of the second day the participants start the build of the file of respondents in the workspace, with `prep/01_build_respondents.R`, and let it finish that evening, so that a check that fails comes to light while the facilitator can still help; the second session of the third day starts from the built file.

::: {.callout-note}
Each session of the first and the third days has a slide deck of its own, written on 6 November 2026 and not yet tried in class, and a module as its reading. The first day teaches R, the IDE and Quarto in the workspace of the Housing and racial bias case study, the running example of the modules, so the participants install it beside the workspace of this case study. The durations are drafts for CM to adjust.
:::

**Day 1 – Open research and the tools.**

| Session | Slides, AR4DS website | Reading | Draft |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Credibility and the three Rs | `slides/credibility.qmd` | the glossary of `resources.qmd` | 75′ |
| 2. SCORE | `slides/score.qmd` | the pages on SCORE and on the robustness article, AR4DS website | 60′ |
| 3. Repositories and data sources | `slides/repositories.qmd` | `companion/data-sources.qmd`, `companion/repositories.qmd` | 60′ |
| 4. R | `slides/r.qmd` | `tools/r.qmd` on the AR4DS website, `companion/intro-r.qmd` | 75′ |
| 5. Positron | `slides/ide.qmd` | `tools/ide.qmd` on the AR4DS website, `companion/ide.qmd` | 45′ |
| 6. Quarto | `slides/quarto.qmd` | `tools/quarto.qmd` on the AR4DS website | 60′ |

**Day 2 – The full-day format**, run as in its own run sheet above. After the first day, Part 1 can take credibility and the robustness study at speed and give the time to Task 1 and Task 2. The day ends with the start of the build, as the section "Before day 3" on the day-2 page sets out: each participant puts the sixteen files in one folder beside the workspace, sources `prep/01_build_respondents.R` before leaving and reports any check that fails, with `data_private/build_report.csv`.

**Day 3 – The methods and your report.**

| Session | Slides | Reading | Draft |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Panel data | `slides/panel-data.qmd` | `companion/panel-data.qmd` | 75′ |
| 2. Multilevel models and the respondents, on the file built after day 2 | `slides/multilevel.qmd` | `companion/multilevel.qmd` | 75′ |
| 3. Bayesian estimation | `slides/bayesian.qmd` | `companion/bayesian.qmd` | 60′ |
| 4. Your report | `slides/report.qmd` | `git-github.qmd` and `tools/quarto.qmd`, AR4DS website | 120′ |

A participant without a file of respondents, because the build failed or the files are missing, follows the second session on the slides: the GESIS terms do not allow a copy of the file to be passed on, so there is no other route.

In the session on the report, each participant opens the workspace, turns its folder into a repository with the completed preregistration block of Task 5 as the first commit, writes the report around the declared analysis, renders it from a clean session and commits each step. The file of respondents stays out of the repository: `data_private/` is ignored by git, and the GESIS terms do not allow it to be shared.

## The self-taught format {#run-self-study}

The self-taught format runs without a facilitator, and each stage page gives the total of its stage and nothing finer, because the time that a stage takes depends on the reader. The stages use the full slide deck of the case study, `slides/full.qmd`, and a semester course can follow the same route in class. What the facilitator can still do for a self-taught cohort is keep the live results pipeline running between deliveries, so that a result submitted alone appears on the Class results page of the case study (`facilitator/live-results-setup.md`).

## Help and ready-to-paste texts {#chat-protocols-and-ready-to-paste-texts}

**Help:** a raised hand is the flag, for a question or for a machine that is stuck. Rescues run by buddy-chunk.

**Silent class:** wait 20 seconds, then name one or two people gently. Two substantive answers from twenty participants are enough to proceed.

**Catch-up card (on screen at the start of Part 3):**

> Just back? You missed nothing you can't recover: (1) if Task 2 is unfinished, keep your estimand statement and come back to it later; (2) Task 3 is the reproduction – choose C6HJR, KQXUE or 018OL, in your workspace or, if your installation failed, in the slides, which have a hint and a full solution for each, and the values on record are −3.804, −7.169 and −1.206; (3) raise your hand and I'll come to you.

---

## Contingencies {#contingency-table}

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| **A participant's webR fails mid-task** | The cheatsheet ladder: hard reload and rerun the cells above, then a second browser, then buddy-chunk on my screen. Last rung: the specification is one row of `data/spec_curve.csv`, which the download button of the chart on the Specification curve page serves; submit it by hand. |
| **The cell of 018OL stalls on its download** | Let it finish on a good connection, or switch the participant to C6HJR or KQXUE, which need nothing beyond the page. |
| **A participant's installation breaks** | Switch them to the slides, opened in a tab of their own, or to the browser lab: both hold every task, and the workspace survives for later. |
| **The live chart fails** | Rung 1: `class-results.qmd` falls back to the committed `data/class_results.csv`. Rung 2: pull the Sheet CSV, commit, re-render locally and share my screen. Rung 3: the static curve of 864 and the reference results are enough for the debrief. |
| **The OSF is slow or unreachable** | Show the dossier and the deposits on my screen. The data never depend on the OSF, because they ship with the browser lab and the workspace. |
| **"How long should this take?"** | Every fit on the 270-row panel is effectively instantaneous: `feols` with two-way or country fixed effects under 0.01 s; `try_spec()` in the workspace, CR2 test included, about 1 s for the first call, which loads the packages, and under 0.1 s after it; `try_spec()` in the browser lab instant, since it reads the curve that ships with the page. A participant who is waiting is waiting for a package download: the browser lab fetches its packages, about 24 MB, once when the page opens, a long moment on poor wifi, and nothing after that, because the Task 2 graph reads its adjustment sets from a table that ships with the page; the first run in the workspace installs the whole package set once. Ask what it is stuck on before assuming that the model is the problem. |
| **My connection drops** | The standing order shown at the start. |
| **Recording objections** | Recording is optional, so stop it. |

## Expected numbers {#answer-keys-and-expected-numbers}

- Warm-up of Task 1: 1 = reproducibility (a failed attempt is still reproducibility); 2 = the grey area between reproducibility and robustness, argued both ways; 3 = replicability; 4 = generalisability.
- **Task 3, C6HJR** (`europeanisation_cy.csv`, two-way fixed effects, conventional errors): b = −0.00347, SE = 0.00091, **t = −3.804**, df = 233, N = 270. Its conventional p is 0.0002, but under the workshop's rule, CR2 errors clustered by country on 9.8 Satterthwaite df, p = 0.0504 (CR1 on 26 df 0.029; `data/display_inference.csv`): not significant at 5% under that rule. Never call it significant without naming the errors.
- **Task 3, KQXUE** (`analyst_KQXUE.csv`, country fixed effects, conventional errors): b = −0.00736, SE = 0.00103, **t = −7.169**, df = 242, N = 270, CI from −0.00938 to −0.00533, as in the write-up of the analyst. With `cosmo_once` (EB 62.0 counted once) t = −7.166. On the Eurostat series as retrieved in 2026, in which Portugal 2013 reads 13.0 rather than 12.9, t = −7.172; the file uses the December 2023 vintage.
- **Task 3, 018OL** (`analyst_018OL.csv`, random intercepts for country, year and wave, Satterthwaite df): on the outcome rescaled to 0–1, b = −0.00203, SE = 0.00169, **t = −1.206**, df = 396.9, N = 420, as in the knitted output of the analyst; on the raw cell means b = −0.00072, SE = 0.00060, with the same t and df. With the year of the fieldwork for EB 79.3, t = −1.606. The default `parameters::model_parameters()` reports the residual df (414); `ci_method = "satterthwaite"` gives 396.9.
- **Hands-on 3b**: KQXUE, `task2.do`, `append using` the temporary file of EB 62.0 on two consecutive lines (441 and 442); 018OL, the line of the R Markdown file that sets `YEA` from the first four characters of the file name, commented "year of data collection"; C6HJR, the comment `# APRIL 2025 - Mistake in dataset here` in the corrected script of the fork. Good checks: no file read twice; one wave per fieldwork period with its expected count; counts by year and country; two builds compared cell by cell.
- The curve (`data/spec_curve.csv`): 864 specifications; 98.1% below zero; 77.2% below zero with CR2 p < 0.05 (conventional 90.3%, CR1 80.1%); claim-aligned r from −0.589 to +0.116, median −0.314. Country fixed effects 92.6% below zero with CR2 p < 0.05, two-way 61.8%.
- Few clusters (`display_inference.csv`): two-way fixed effects t = −3.80 on 233 df conventional, −2.31 on 26 df with CR1 (p = 0.029), −2.23 on 9.8 df with CR2 (p = 0.0504); country fixed effects on the country-year panel t = −6.87 on 242 df, −3.62 on 26 df, −3.51 on 8.5 df (p = 0.0072). Within and between (`display_between_within.csv`): −0.0056 within, +0.0041 across the 27 country means (p = 0.31), difference p = 0.024.
- Reference results (`data/reference_marks.csv`), each placed on the degrees of freedom of its own inference, with the number of the 864 further below zero: KEVF1 −0.452 (147); KQXUE −0.419 (214); OA −0.385 (267, the refit of its design without the education interactions, t = −8.39 on 403.9 Satterthwaite df); C6HJR −0.242 (583); PRL47 −0.176 (740); 018OL −0.060 (833). The robustness study recorded PRL47 at −0.006, its z converted on 394,575 respondents.
- Fork importance (`spec_curve_forks.csv`), share of the variance: estimator 41.5%, predictor 16.9, outcome 9.0, adjustment 4.3, item set 3.1, no-opinion rule 0.9, series 0.1, cell weighting 0.0, form 0.0, interactions 24.1.
- Placement of the reproduced specification (for participants without their own submission): 67%, with 583 of the 864 further below zero.

## Debrief questions {#debrief-question-bank}

Choose by what the class actually produced, not by the order below.

1. **The three reproductions**: "Three analysts, one claim, the same instructions: −1.2, −3.8, −7.2. Which difference between their models matters most, and how would you find out?"
2. **The slips**: "None of the three slips changed a conclusion. Does that make them unimportant? What would have to be true of a slip for it to matter?"
3. **The vintage**: "A public series changed after the analysis. Whose job is it to keep the version that a result rests on?"
4. **Decision that moved most**: "Before I showed the decomposition – which decision did you bet on, and what made the estimator carry so much?"
5. **Justification quality**: "Whose graph settled their choice? Whose graph could have justified three different specifications equally well?"
6. **Preregistration felt**: "Did completing the block before running change how the result felt when it landed?"
7. **The inference gap**: "If a curve-level permutation test came back at p = .30, what would survive of today? What if it came back at p = .004?"

- [ ] After a workshop, run the reset procedure at the top of this guide.
- [ ] Export the feedback form responses.
- [ ] Improvement log: which segment ran longest; how the class split between the three analysts of Task 3, and how long the download of 018OL took on the connections of the class; whether the estimand statements showed real spread; how many people had the workspace running, and what that changed; which rungs of the contingency ladders fired.
